text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: HIGH - region=us-west-az3, service=inference-serving, symptom=pod-saturation -> paging on-call

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Triggered by policy 'az3-serving-latency' - incident id PD-98341 - auto-escalation in 10m

Amber: acked. I'm on it. grabbing logs and look at autoscaler.

Samir: @Amber thanks. quick note — customers on dedicated pools may see 5xx or slow token streams. any expected cluster maintenance?

Amber: not scheduled. first glance shows node evictions spike in az3 about 06:12 UTC.

Mira: tagging network team FYI, but looks noisy from kube-scheduler evictions and OOMs on the inference runtime pods.

Chao: @Mira sending current node list + pod statuses:
```
kubectl get nodes -o wide --selector=region=us-west,az=az3
NAME           STATUS   ROLES    AGE    VERSION
node-az3-001   Ready    gpu      52d    v1.24.7
node-az3-002   NotReady gpu      6h     v1.24.7
node-az3-003   Ready    gpu      34d    v1.24.7
```
and pods for model-serving namespace:
```
kubectl -n model-serving get pods -o wide | grep az3
inference-0   CrashLoopBackOff  5/5  0.3  node-az3-002
inference-1   Running           5/5  0.6  node-az3-001
```

Amber: node-az3-002 shows OOMKilled for the runtime container. raw log tail:
```
E 06:11:32 runtime: allocation failed: cannot allocate chunk 12G for kv-cache
I 06:11:36 kernel: killed process pid=7234 (runtime) due to OOM
```

Amber: action plan: 1) activate regional fallback routing to az2 for new requests, 2) scale up replacement nodes in az3, 3) throttle batch queue to reduce mem pressure.

Alex: +1 on fallback. Alex from Routing: I'll flip the routing policy to prefer az2 for 15m and set short TTL so we can revert once healthy. Doing canary in 1min.

Ops-SRE: @Amber when you flip fallback, ensure warm cache tags are cleared for the routed path to avoid serving stale KV artifacts.

Mira: triggering autoscale group +2 nodes in az3 now (request submitted to cloud). ETA ~4m.

Amber: enabling throttling on batch-queue: set BATCH_MAX_BYTES=2GB and reduce max_batch_window to 50ms. Pushing config:
```yaml
service:
  batch:
    max_bytes: 2147483648
    max_window_ms: 50
```

Samir: customer impact note: preliminary checks show 12 customers on dedicated pools had elevated 5xx rates between 06:10-06:18 UTC; no full downtime but degraded latency >5s. I'll open a short CS ticket and notify affected accounts after we confirm fallbacks.

Leo (CS): please include customer-safe wording, we may want to say 'service experienced increased latency for some requests in us-west-az3; automated failover reduced impact'.

incident-bot: PD-98341: Amber acknowledged. Escalation timer paused.

Amber: Alex - routing flip done. Commands executed:
```
redwood-routing set-pref --from az3 --to az2 --ttl 900 --policy=prefer-capacity
Response: ok, change propagated to edge-proxies in 22s
```

Alex: seeing traffic shift; percentage served from az2 jumped to ~48% within 30s. latency tail dropping.

Chao: new nodes coming up, kube join logs show provisioning ok. Starting kube-proxy health checks.

Mira: node-az3-004 is Ready. Scheduling pods back, but we'll keep throttles for 10m to let caches warm gradually.

Amber: I'm running a quick diag across runtimes to confirm KV cache integrity. If no corruption, we will drain the transient node-az3-002 and cordon it for deeper investigation.

Samir: pulling metrics for 5xx and tail latency. Preliminary: 5xx rate peaked at 3.4% at 06:15 then decayed to 0.7% post-routing flip. Token generation P99 went from 8.2s -> 1.1s.

Leo (CS): drafting customer note: short update with ETA to full health (monitoring for 30m). Will coordinate with Samir for affected list.

Amber: cordon + drain node-az3-002 now to stop noisy restarts:
```
kubectl cordon node-az3-002
kubectl drain node-az3-002 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

Chao: drain completed. Pod evictions completed gracefully or re-scheduled. No crash loops observed on new placements.

incident-bot: Monitoring checkpoints: autoscaler:+2 nodes success, routing fallback active, batch throttle applied. Next automated check in 5m.

Amber: next steps: keep fallback for 15m, keep throttle for 10m, run postmortem if root cause is resource leak. Assigning oncall post-incident: Samir to lead RCA, Mira to assist on SIG runtime, Chao for infra notes.

Samir: acknowledged as RCA owner. I'll capture events and collect heap dumps from runtime pods that experienced OOM.

Mira: will run load replay to validate fix once we restore normal routing.

Alex: will revert routing after we verify stable metrics for 10m.

Leo (CS): customer note queued, will send once we have stable window.

Amber: closing alert for now but keeping thread for 30m watch. If anything regresses, page will re-fire. Thanks all. :heart:

incident-bot: PD-98341: incident status -> mitigated (auto-ack by handler).

Ops-SRE: thumbs up. Quick follow-up: create incident ticket and include node dumps + allocation metrics. I'll add runbook pointers.

Samir: will produce preliminary RCA in the ticket within 24h.

Amber: handing off watch to Ops-SRE for the next 30m. Oncall handoff: @Ops-SRE you're now primary for this incident.

Ops-SRE: acknowledged. Monitoring.

(30m later) Amber: follow-up note: system stabilized, routing returned to normal at 07:05 UTC. no customer escalations opened. ticket PD-98341 -> INC-2026-az3-oom assigned for full RCA.

Leo (CS): sent customers a brief note at 07:12 UTC.

Samir: filing heap dumps and initial traces in the incident ticket.

incident-bot: thread closed due to inactivity.
